subject: Contract tether: proposed short-term bridging plan for close slippage
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jane Roberts <jane.roberts@stellarhealth.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contract tether: proposed short-term bridging plan for close slippage

Hi Jane / Amit —

Thanks again for the candid sync this morning. I know StellarHealth is laser-focused on the Oct 31 production target; from our side we want to keep momentum while we work through procurement and the final SOW. Attached is a short-term bridging proposal I promised: a 6-week mutual action plan (MAP v3) that preserves your evaluation milestones while deferring formal contract start until procurement signs the SOW. High-level: 

- Temporary evaluation credit pool to cover the pilot (covers inference usage through initial go-live)
- Staged SOW: signature on the core terms now, full commercial SOW to follow procurement approvals
- Two-week tech canary with roll-forward guardrails (Marcus detailed below)
- Security items: we'll commit to expedited answers on your questionnaire within 3 business days

Next steps I propose: we share MAP v3 with your procurement/legal today, Marcus runs the canary run plan by your infra team tomorrow, and I loop in Prioyom for onboarding readiness next week. If you agree, I’ll seed a DocuSign for the tethered SOW and circulate the MAP as a tracked doc.

Attachments: MAP_StellarHealth_v3.pdf (MAP), SOW_StellarHealth_draft_20251007.docx (stub), pricing-bridge-2025.xlsx (estimates)

Thanks — I want to be pragmatic here and avoid losing the Oct window.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwood.com)
Redwood Inference

From: Jane Roberts <jane.roberts@stellarhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@stellarhealth.com>, procurement@stellarhealth.com
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract tether: proposed short-term bridging plan for close slippage

Rachel —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the MAP. A few quick clarifying Qs from procurement/legal: 

1) What specifically is the "temporary evaluation credit pool" — is it a discount, a credit on invoice, or a deferred invoicing mechanism? We need a legal-safe construct.
2) The staged SOW sounds workable but procurement needs a concrete cutoff date when the tether converts to a standard contract. Can you propose a hard date?
3) We will need the security questionnaire responses before the canary if possible (we have a compliance review next Thursday).

Amit is supportive of the canary but wants confirmation the canary won't interfere with our production telemetry. Marcus — can you share the runbook and expected telemetry footprint?

If we can get answers to the above today, procurement will prioritize the tethered signature.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Roberts
VP, Procurement — StellarHealth
(attachment: formal_req_list.pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Jane Roberts <jane.roberts@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract tether: proposed short-term bridging plan for close slippage

Jane / Rachel —

Quick technical note on the canary:

- Canary approach: 2-week rolling canary with a single tenant slice (non-prod namespace) mirroring a 10% traffic sample from the test harness.
- Expected telemetry: +12-15% write volume to our observability sink for the duration; negligible CPU delta on your side (we only sample inference calls).
- Safeguards: auto-fallback to the baseline model and throttling rules if latency increases beyond 150ms p95.
- Runbook: start at 00:00 UTC following a 24h blackout approval window; daily checkpoints with your infra; immediate rollback on error.

I attached a one-page runbook stub (canary-runbook-stub.pdf). If you accept, we’ll expand to a full runbook and schedule a 30-minute tech review tomorrow.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: canary-runbook-stub.pdf)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jane Roberts <jane.roberts@stellarhealth.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Prioyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract tether: proposed short-term bridging plan for close slippage

Jane / Amit —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Answers inline below and I’ve also attached an annotated MAP with dates filled in (MAP_StellarHealth_v3.pdf).

1) Temporary evaluation credit pool — operationally this is a pre-funded credit that is consumed against usage. Legally we phrase it as a "pilot credit" applied to invoices; it does not alter the SOW commercial terms and will be reconciled on signature of the full SOW. Procurement/legal can elect an escrow-style hold if that simplifies your risk posture.

2) Staged SOW cutoff — propose Nov 21, 2025 as the conversion date (6 weeks from tether start). If procurement needs a different cadence, we can shift, but we need a committed conversion date to trigger billing reconciliation.

3) Security questionnaire — we will provide prioritized responses to the 10 highest-risk items within 48 hours; full questionnaire within 5 business days.

Action items (from MAP v3):
- Oct 8: Tech review and canary schedule (Marcus / Amit)
- Oct 10: Procurement review of tether language and sign-off on pilot credit mechanism
- Oct 13–24: Two-week canary + 1-week monitoring window
- Nov 21: Conversion to full SOW (target date)

If that looks acceptable I’ll issue the DocuSign for the tethered SOW today and Prioyom will prep onboarding readiness notes for the canary.

Rachel
(attachment: MAP_StellarHealth_v3.pdf, SOW_StellarHealth_draft_20251007.docx)

From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@stellarhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Jane Roberts <jane.roberts@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@stellarhealth.com
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract tether: proposed short-term bridging plan for close slippage

Rachel / Team —

We reviewed the MAP and Marcus's canary notes with our infra leads. We can greenlight the canary under two conditions: 1) full answers to the top-10 security items before Oct 13 and 2) a hard kill-switch in the runbook that we control. Marcus — can you add an infra-controlled kill-switch to the runbook (manual and API kill)?

Procurement is comfortable with the Nov 21 conversion date if the tethered signature happens by Oct 10. Jane — happy to push procurement hard if legal gets the tether language today.

Amit
Amit Shah | CTO, StellarHealth

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Prioyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Roberts <jane.roberts@stellarhealth.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@stellarhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Contract tether: proposed short-term bridging plan for close slippage — escalation / exec ask

Laura / Team —

Looping you in for short exec approval. Quick summary: StellarHealth risk-logged that procurement gating could push our close beyond Oct 31. To preserve their production window we proposed a tethered MAP (attached). Customer requires: top-10 security answers by Oct 13, an infra-controlled kill-switch in the canary, and a tether signature by Oct 10 to hit Nov 21 conversion.

Requesting: a one-time 10% pilot credit (applied as pre-funded credit) and authorization to accept the Nov 21 conversion cadence with the tether. This is intended as a retention/enablement concession to prevent deal slip and preserve trajectory to expansion.

Why approve: Failure to approve risks losing Oct go-live and elongates procurement cycles; approving preserves momentum and positions us for expansion in H1 2026.

Attachments (for exec review): MAP_StellarHealth_v3.pdf, pricing-bridge-2025.xlsx, SOW_StellarHealth_draft_20251007.docx

—Rachel
(onward: short one-line approvals expected)
